driverRegime.method: daily % change of each asset regressed on the daily change in the US 2-year and 10-year yields (basis points) and on the daily % change in WTI; a driver is dominant when |corr| >= 0.4

dataNotes: Run timing: this cycle ran the morning of 19 October 2026 after the GitHub Actions fetch job drafted contracts/*.2026-10-16.json from Friday 16 October's close. Every figure used is dated at or before the 2026-10-16 close; documents/live.json and news-log entries dated 19 October were NOT used.

Bonds, dollar and IWM sigma are not auto-fetched and were carried stale from the prior board (bonds TLT IV 15, 25 September; dollar EUR/USD 1M IV 4.72, 21 September; IWM RVX 19.97, 23 September). No newer prints were obtained.

News-log entries for 2026-10-16 (six) were confirmed identical to those in the Artifact database; no hand-entered issue entries were dated 16 October. Percentage changes are computed from the drafted 15 and 16 October closes. Cash-index levels, yields, oil and data surprises come from the news log as written; no separate web search was run, to keep the blindness rule clean.

The news log carries two fed-pricing statements that sit awkwardly together: October hike odds near 50/50 after CPI/PPI (15 October entry) and Fed-on-hold odds of about 85% on CME FedWatch (16 October entry); the Fed-path votes cite the hot data and flag the discrepancy rather than pick a side on pricing.
No 16 October high-yield OAS, MOVE, breadth count, positioning print, sentiment survey or seasonal statistic was obtained; those category votes are neutral.

newsLog.event: US stock futures point higher Friday as Bessent steps up economic pressure on Iran and Treasury yields cool
newsLog.numbers: Futures levels n/a; Fed on hold odds ~85% (CME FedWatch); ex-auto/gas retail sales +0.2%, control group +0.1%
newsLog.reaction: Dow, S&P 500 and Nasdaq 100 futures were higher pre-market after Thursday's higher close, with yields cooling and Q3 earnings (TSMC, Alcoa, IBKR) in focus. Soft retail-sales control group and a likely Fed hold support the rates-relief tone.
newsLog.tickers: SPY, S&P, QQQ, Nasdaq, TLT, 10Y, yield

newsLog.event: Brent steady near $105 in early Friday trade as Iran oil-revenue squeeze continues
newsLog.numbers: Brent ~$105.46 (-0.21%) at 02:15 UTC; WTI -1.74% per Vantage
newsLog.reaction: Oil still carries a large geopolitical premium amid the US blockade of Iranian exports and sanctions on the shadow fleet; early-session moves were modest and not a clear directional catalyst for the open.

newsLog.event: Stocks sink as S&P 500 and Nasdaq post steep losses on tech-led selloff
newsLog.reaction: Nasdaq and small caps led declines as tech/AI names sold off while the Dow held up relatively better; for the week S&P -1.95%, Nasdaq -4.48%, Dow +0.67%, and the 10-yr yield fell ~14.6bp, its biggest weekly drop since mid-February.

newsLog.event: AI bubble fears deepen as CoreWeave slides toward 11.8% intraday on $50B debt load; semis extend losing streak
newsLog.numbers: CoreWeave intraday -11.8%; Philadelphia Semiconductor Index (SOX) fell for an 8th straight session, SOXX -12.6% from its Oct 2 close
newsLog.reaction: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang pushed back on the fears, saying CoreWeave's cost of capital is actually decreasing; investors remain focused on whether upcoming Big Tech earnings show AI capex converting into revenue and cash flow.

newsLog.event: Oil jumps to multi-month highs as Saudi-led coalition intercepts missiles and NATO weighs response to Black Sea drone attacks
newsLog.numbers: WTI (Dec) $99.02 (+$2.52, +2.61%), highest close since Sept 17; Brent $109.86 (+$3.94), highest since May 19
newsLog.reaction: Early signals of Iranian openness to dialogue had briefly eased prices, but renewed reports of military escalation reversed the move; energy stocks outperformed amid the broader equity selloff.

newsLog.event: September import prices and industrial output top forecasts, reinforcing a sticky-inflation narrative after this week's CPI/PPI beats
newsLog.numbers: Import prices +1.1% (vs +0.8% exp); industrial production +0.7% (vs +0.4% exp); Sept CPI +0.6% m/m, 3.7% y/y (vs 3.6% exp), core CPI 2.6% y/y; Sept PPI +1.3%, core PPI +0.3%
newsLog.reaction: A week of hotter-than-expected inflation prints (CPI Tue, PPI/retail sales/jobless claims Thu, import prices/industrial output Fri) tempered bets on near-term Fed easing and pressured rate-sensitive growth and AI stocks, even as the 10-yr yield still fell on the week.
